Question ID: GEO_U03_L03_GP_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.1; MLA.GEO.TRI.3 (readiness support)

If triangle ABC ≅ triangle DEF, which vertex corresponds to B?

feedback.text: B and E are in the second position, so they correspond.
D corresponds to A, not B.
F corresponds to C, not B.
A is in the first triangle and corresponds to D.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L03_GP_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.1; MLA.GEO.TRI.3 (readiness support)

If triangle PQR ≅ triangle XYZ, which side corresponds to QR?

feedback.text: XY corresponds to PQ.
QR uses the second and third vertices, so it corresponds to YZ.
XZ corresponds to PR.
PQ is in the first triangle, not the corresponding side in the second.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L03_GP_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.1; MLA.GEO.TRI.3 (readiness support)

If triangle LMN ≅ triangle RST, which angle corresponds to angle N?

feedback.text: R corresponds to L.
S corresponds to M.
N and T are in the third position, so they correspond.
L is a vertex in the first triangle.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L03_GP_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.1; MLA.GEO.TRI.3 (readiness support)

Which congruence statement correctly matches A to D, B to E, and C to F?

feedback.text: This matches B to F and C to E.
This matches A to E, not D.
This reverses several corresponding vertices.
The vertices are listed in matching order: A-D, B-E, C-F.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L03_GP_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.1; MLA.GEO.TRI.3 (readiness support)

What information is needed before concluding two figures are congruent?

answer.text: Evidence that corresponding sizes and shapes match.

feedback.text: Congruence requires same size and shape supported by evidence.

answer.text: They are drawn near each other.

feedback.text: Location on the page does not prove congruence.
Color is not a geometric property for congruence.

answer.text: They look similar at a glance.

feedback.text: Appearance alone is not enough evidence.
